blocks.x: Event Horizon Officially Returns In August 2027 After 30-Year Wait

Nicholas Becher is a gaming journalist with an MFA in Creative Writing from FAU. With extensive experience playing video games, he covers all forms of gaming content at Screen Rant, from breaking news to the latest fan theories. Most-played games range from Clair Obscur to Civ to Elden Ring to Halo 2 and beyond.

The fact it's been nearly 30 years since Paul W.S. Anderson's cult classic Event Horizon first released is a bit hard to believe, especially considering the film never saw a reboot or proper sequel in all that time. While the Event Horizon: Inferno comics have been a hit among hardcore fans, and the newly announced Pandemonium prequel comic will give us some unique new insights into the famous Gravity Drive from the film, many fans are still waiting for an update on the supposed TV series in development at Amazon, especially as the original film's 30th anniversary creeps up on us next year.

The film still holds up as one of the most unique space horror films of all time, with Sam Neill and Laurence Fishburne delivering two memorable performances that stand out as high points in their historical careers. And while it's not exactly the epic return fans have been hoping for, after a 30-year wait, Event Horizon is making an official return in August 2027 to celebrate its monumental anniversary (via Titan).
Event Horizon Officially Returns With 30th Anniversary Release

While it isn't the cinematic sequel or TV series update fans have been hoping for, the original Event Horizon is receiving a major new release in 2027. Publisher Titan Books has announced Event Horizon: The Making of the Classic Film, an extensive behind-the-scenes retrospective arriving on August 24, 2027, just nine days after the 30th anniversary on August 15.

Written by Janine Pipe, the hardcover release will span a whopping 192 pages, with a list price of $50 in the United States and £39.99 in the United Kingdom. Pre-orders are currently listed through retailers listed on Titan Books' official website, though they haven't gone live yet on sites such as Amazon.

The book promises a comprehensive look at how Anderson's nightmarish sci-fi adventure came together, featuring rare archival materials, previously unpublished production photographs, original storyboards, and exclusive new interviews with members of the cast and crew. Most importantly, Anderson himself is directly involved in the project and will contribute an intro, giving fans access to the filmmaker's perspective on the movie's production its cult status over the past 30 years.

Pipe is also no stranger to cult horror, having previously written behind-the-scenes books exploring Dog Soldiers and The Descent. Given Event Horizon's famously troubled production, including substantial material removed before its theatrical release, there's certainly no shortage of fascinating history to explore. However, there's currently no indication that the book will include any recovered footage from the film's notoriously graphic deleted scenes.

blocks.x: This unique insider look at Event Horizon is sure to spark some hope about whether it could become part of a larger 30th-anniversary celebration. It's worth noting, however, that Event Horizon: The Making of the Classic Film was originally scheduled to drop this year before being pushed back to August 2027. Nevertheless, there's already some precedent for a larger revival, particularly considering an Event Horizon television adaptation was announced as being in development at Amazon back in 2019.

Director Adam Wingard was attached to the project and, in a March 2024 interview with Inverse, confirmed that an impressive script existed, although the series had yet to gain momentum. Its eventual fate remains unclear, with no confirmed premiere date or series order.

“It’s definitely in the works ... I’ve just been in Godzilla land for so long. I wouldn’t say that there’s definitive traction in terms of it moving forward, but we have a f****** amazing script. Once this movie’s over, it’s just about refocusing my attention towards getting that set up.” - Adam Wingard in a 2024 interview with Inverse

Of course, not every Event Horizon fan necessarily wants to see the franchise revived on-screen. Some would undoubtedly welcome an opportunity to explore the terrifying mythology behind the Gravity Drive, while others believe the original film works best as a standalone experience, with its many unanswered questions arguably being a key reason for the film's enduring legacy.

There's obviously no guarantee Event Horizon will see the same success as recent sci-fi reboots of older IPs, and the upcoming book itself isn't evidence of anything in and of itself. Nevertheless, with the franchise already seeing a resurgence through its recent comics, a major anniversary on-screen return wouldn't be all that surprising. Whether anything bigger materializes remains to be seen, but the 30th anniversary would certainly be the perfect opportunity to revisit one of science fiction's most disturbing cult-classic universes.
